summary: Built M2-S01 (access, design-only, owner metadata-builder) into four artefacts: the CustomPermission Bypass_Case_Intake_Validation, the PermissionSet Case_Intake_Integration that grants it and nothing else, a two-type package.xml at API 62.0, and deploy-order.md. Every element written comes from the Step 3 inventory built out of admin/custom-permissions references/metadata-examples.md § 2 and § 5 and admin/permission-set-architecture references/metadata-examples.md § 1, § 2 and § 5. Both declared checkers exited 0 on the first pass with zero findings, the two cited-skill checkers that ship one were also run, all three XML files parse, and check-outputs returned ok. The step's outputs are a custom permission and a permission set — no Profile — so no layoutAssignments or recordTypeVisibilities are written here; deploy-order.md records that M2-S03 carries the profile layout assignments that M1 report finding F-01 needs, with the exact Case.Support / Case.Billing and Case-Case Support Layout / Case-Case Billing Layout member forms taken from artefacts/M1-S02/deploy-order.md.
confidence_rationale: Step 10: HIGH on four of its five conditions — every emitted element traced to the Step 3 inventory, both declared checkers exited 0 on the first pass, check-outputs returned ok, and every declared output was written with nothing outside artefacts/M2-S01/. MEDIUM because the fifth is not met: two Questions-to-Ask rows were answered from a documented skill default rather than from the plan (custom-permissions' expiry row and permission-set-architecture's activation row), and one row — 'which contexts read it' — was answered from a downstream step's declared outputs (M3-S01) rather than from an answered clarification.

dimensions_skipped.reason: Two of the fourteen deduplicated Questions-to-Ask rows were answered from the cited skill's own documented default rather than from plan.json: 'Is the grant permanent, or should it expire?' (custom-permissions) and 'Does any permission need step-up activation?' (permission-set-architecture, answered false per its § 1 note). Neither is a query failure; neither clarification exists in the plan's 97 questions.

admin/validation-rules is cited on the step and ships check_validation_rules.py, which exits 1 at --manifest-dir artefacts/M2-S01 with 'no validation rule metadata files found'. That is the checker firing on an empty scope, not on a defect: this step declares no validation-rule output and writing one to satisfy it would widen the step past outputs[]. It is not one of the step's declared acceptance tests, and no repair pass was spent on it.

process_observations.observation: Both declared checkers exited 0 on the first pass with zero findings, so no repair pass was needed and the three-pass ceiling in Step 8 was not approached.

check_access_model.py returns 1 on ANY finding (emit_result, script line 152-160), so its exit 0 here is a stronger statement than a severity threshold would be: the permission set carries no dangerous system permission, no profile-only element, and no object grant at all.

reports/MILESTONE-M1-REPORT.md finding F-01 and its go/no-go list both name M2-S01 as the step that carries layoutAssignments ('layoutAssignments is M2-S01's'), but in plan version 5 M2-S01's outputs[] contains no Profile — the profiles are M2-S03's, whose title is 'Minimal base profiles carrying only default app, default record type and layout assignment'. The report was written against an earlier step numbering and its remedy now points at the wrong step id.

The declared output path names the permission set Case_Intake_Integration, while templates/admin/permission-set-patterns.md gives integration bundles the form Integration_<System>_Bundle and feature sets Feat_<Feature>; the step's templates[] is empty, so no template was cited to resolve the divergence and the declared path was written as-is.

Nothing on file says where the Email-to-Case / Web-to-Case identity gets ApiEnabled, and this permission set deliberately does not grant it — the step's own manual acceptance test requires the set to grant the custom permission and nothing else, and ApiEnabled is in check_access_model.py's DANGEROUS_PERMISSIONS, so granting it here would fail the step's second declared checker.
The step is built and its four declared outputs exist; the molecular tests it declares have not been run by this agent.

decision_record.question: What exactly does holding this permission let someone do, in one sentence?
decision_record.answer: Save a Case that the Case intake validation rules would reject, because it was created through the API by Email-to-Case or Web-to-Case.

decision_record.question: Which contexts read it — validation rule, formula, Flow, Apex, LWC, component visibility?
decision_record.answer: Validation rule only. M3-S01 declares exactly two consumers: Case.Priority_Required_On_Agent_Save and Case.Origin_Must_Be_Known, each carrying NOT($Permission.Bypass_Case_Intake_Validation).
decision_record.source: upstream/downstream artefact — plan.json steps[M3-S01].outputs[] and inputs.note

decision_record.question: Does anything already hold this access through a profile?
decision_record.answer: No. build_mode is design-only and no Profile exists anywhere under artefacts/; the grant is authored on a permission set, which is the skill's own instruction (gotcha 1).
decision_record.source: step inputs + repo scan of artefacts/

decision_record.question: Does another custom permission have to be on for this one to make sense?
decision_record.answer: No — nothing in requirement.md or the answered clarifications names a second gate.

decision_record.question: Who revokes it, and what proves it was revoked?
decision_record.answer: The Security architect (owner_role recorded on Q56 and Q10). Proof is the SetupEntityAccess -> PermissionSetAssignment query, not a metadata diff (gotcha 8).
decision_record.element: description text on both files + the 'Post-deploy step' section of deploy-order.md

decision_record.question: Is this a bypass? If so, which named rules does it suppress?
decision_record.answer: Yes. The two M3-S01 rules are named in the description rather than left as an unnamed org-wide off switch.

decision_record.question: Is the grant permanent, or should it expire?
decision_record.answer: Permanent. DEFAULT — no clarification covers expiry, and the grant is to a standing automated-process identity rather than a data-fix window, which is the case the skill's Temp_<Purpose> / permission-set-expiration route exists for.
decision_record.source: skill default (admin/custom-permissions Questions row; admin/permission-set-expiration named but not invoked)
decision_record.element: no ExpirationDate is expressible in metadata anyway — PermissionSetAssignment is record data

decision_record.question: Which user or permission set license does every person in this persona hold?
decision_record.answer: LicenseId left empty. Q8 answers this explicitly for the build's permission sets, and the population here is one automated-process identity whose licence is not on file.
decision_record.source: clarification Q8 (via the deduplicated Questions list; Q10 confirms the model is additive)

decision_record.question: Which objects does this capability touch, and at what CRUD level?
decision_record.answer: None. The set is a pure feature-access slice; the step's manual acceptance test requires no objectPermissions and no fieldPermissions.
decision_record.source: step inputs + the step's own acceptance_tests[4]

decision_record.question: Does anything here need View All Records or Modify All Records?
decision_record.element: no objectPermissions at all, so no viewAllRecords/modifyAllRecords

decision_record.question: Is this bundle for a named person or for a standing role that changes people?
decision_record.answer: A standing non-human identity — the Email-to-Case / Web-to-Case automated process. Recorded in the description and in deploy-order.md as a post-deploy assignment with a named owner.

decision_record.question: Does any permission need step-up activation?
decision_record.answer: No. DEFAULT — hasActivationRequired false, which is what the skill's § 1 and § 2 examples carry 'on purpose' and what the § 3 note requires of anything destined for a PSG.

decision_record.question: Who checks the group after deploy, and against which user?
decision_record.answer: Not applicable — this step writes no PermissionSetGroup, so there is no recalculation state machine to poll. M2-S02 owns the PSGs.

decision_record.question: Which users and integrations must be able to save a record the rule would reject?
decision_record.answer: The Email-to-Case and Web-to-Case identity, through this custom permission on this permission set. This is Q56 verbatim and it is why the step exists at all.
